messages.subject: Error because of model format problem (lack of new lines for each equation)?
parts:
Hello,

I feel a bit stupid, but I can't come up with a solution to my problem.
I am using lavaan to model a certain structural equation.
I have the follwing things: 
____________________________________________________

Lat_names= ("Gout","Texture", "Noteglobale")

(Names of the latent variables)


> colnames(Produit1)
[1] "NOM.PRODUIT.HEDO"                             "Note.globale"                                
[3] "Colle.en.bouche"                              "A.le.gout.caractéristique.d.un.emmental"     
[5] "A.un.gout.complexe"                           "A.une.texture.granuleuse..friable"           
[7] "A.le.gout.d.un.emmental.qui.a.eu.le.temps.de" "A.une.texture.caoutchouteuse"

> Produit1_blocks

[[2]]

[[3]]

Texture        0       0           0
Noteglobale    1       1           0

This describes the casual links between latent variables.

Those are almost all obtained with user input

_______________________________________________________

I then use the following code: 



for (k in 1:length(Lat_names)) {
  t=colnames(Produit1)[Produit1_blocks[[k]][1]]
  if (k==1) {
    if (length(Produit1_blocks[[1]])!=1) {

        t=paste(t,"+",colnames(Produit1)[Produit1_blocks[[1]][i]])
      }
    }
    u=paste(" ",Lat_names[k],"=~"," ",t," ")
  }
  else {
    if (length(Produit1_blocks[[k]])!=1) {
      for (i in 2:length(Produit1_blocks[[1]])) {
        t=paste(t,"+",colnames(Produit1)[Produit1_blocks[[k]][i]])
      }
      
    }
    t=paste(Lat_names[k]," ","=~"," ",t," ")    
    u=paste(" ",u," ",t)  
  }
}
#Modèle interne
for (i in 1:sqrt(length(Produit1_path))) {
  for (j in 1:sqrt(length(Produit1_path))) {
    if (Produit1_path[3*i-3+j]==1) {
      u=paste(u,"    ",colnames(Produit1_path)[j],"~",colnames(Produit1_path)[i],"    ")
      print(i)
      print(j)
    }
  }
}

To get this:

> u
[1] "      Gout =~   A.le.gout.caractéristique.d.un.emmental + A.un.gout.complexe + A.le.gout.d.un.emmental.qui.a.eu.le.temps.de     Texture   =~   Colle.en.bouche + A.une.texture.granuleuse..friable  + A.une.texture.caoutchouteuse     Noteglobale   =~   Note.globale        Noteglobale ~ Gout           Noteglobale ~ Texture     "


which looks like a model that could then be fitted using sem() right?
But I get the following error:

> model <- u
> fit <- sem(model, data=Produit1)

Error in ~A.le.gout.caractéristique.d.un.emmental + A.un.gout.complexe +  : 
  object 'A.le.gout.caractéristique.d.un.emmental' not found


What works:

If I type the model straight into the script, with the following format it works perfectly fine.

u="Gout =~  A.le.gout.caractéristique.d.un.emmental + A.un.gout.complexe + A.le.gout.d.un.emmental.qui.a.eu.le.temps.de
Texture =~  Colle.en.bouche + A.une.texture.granuleuse..friable + A.une.texture.caoutchouteuse 
Gout =~ Note.globale 
Texture =~  Note.globale" 

_______________

Conclusion: The one that works is almost exactly the same as the one that doesn't work. BUT the one that works has a new line for each new "equation" of the model, and not the one I get by using my 
paste code. Thus I assume that you need new lines to make it work, and that just spaces between the equations will make it fail? 

Does anyone have an idea how I could adapt my code to get the model written down into the format that I need to get it to work? I have no idea how I can force the storage of new lines for each equation in the variable u

Regards, 

Joël

messages.subject: Re: Error because of model format problem (lack of new lines for each equation)?
parts:
Good morning,

I tried several other things, and I was able to fix my problem. 


What I did not know is that the following actually works: 

u= "Gout =~   A.le.gout.caractéristique.d.un.emmental + A.un.gout.complexe + A.le.gout.d.un.emmental.qui.a.eu.le.temps.de     Texture   =~   Colle.en.bouche + A.une.texture.granuleuse..friable  + A.une.texture.caoutchouteuse      Noteglobale   =~   Note.globale         Noteglobale ~ Gout            Noteglobale ~ Texture     "


The sem() function reads that as if it was written in multiple lines, and doesn't just read as if it was text like the print() function for example. 
Thus, changing my code to add where needed fixed my problem.

Regards, 

Joël

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Error because of model format problem (lack of new lines for each equation)?
parts: > Thus, changing my code to add \n where needed fixed my problem.

Indeed, an explicit "\n" is needed to create a new line. An alternative
is to use ";" which you can use to have several formulas on the same line.

Yves.
